decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 11-0.

changes.quote: The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have improved in recent months but continue to be affected by COVID-19.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have improved in recent months, but the summer's rise in COVID-19 cases has slowed their recovery.”

changes.quote: Job gains have been solid in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic and the reopening of the economy have continued to contribute to elevated levels of inflation.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic and the reopening of the economy have contributed to sizable price increases in some sectors.”

changes.quote: Inflation is elevated, largely reflecting factors that are expected to be transitory.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Risks to the economic outlook remain, including from new variants of the virus.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Risks to the economic outlook remain.”

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses.
In support of these goals, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

In light of inflation developments and the further improvement in the labor market, the Committee decided to reduce the monthly pace of its net asset purchases by $20 billion for Treasury securities and $10 billion for agency mortgage-backed securities.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.54% APR costs about $60.58 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.47% and moved +3 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.11% would rise by about $4.90 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 639k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 6.9% over the past year (November 2021); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 4.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +2 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 1.63%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.16% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 18%, cut 0%, hike 82%.
